subject: Post-call recap: Finlytics perf & economics — proposed tests and timelines
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: James Liao <james.liao@finlytics.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Finlytics perf & economics — proposed tests and timelines

Thanks for your time earlier, James — quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan.

What we covered (short):
- Demoed Redwood hosted endpoint (gpt-style 7B variant) and Dedicated footprint options.
- Walked through routing/fallback, prefix cache behavior, and batching knobs in Redwood Console.
- Rough unit economics in conversation and what drives per-1M token cost (batching, cache hit rate, quantization).

Preliminary Redwood vs hyperscaler differentiation (summary):
- Redwood: unified API across hosted/dedicated/private + built-in KV/prefix caching and auto-batching tuned per workload. Predictable fallbacks to quantized model variants.
- Hyperscalers (managed endpoints): comparable raw throughput for single-model endpoints but usually higher per-token unit costs once you include autoscaling headroom and egress; less built-in prefix caching — customers typically build app-layer caches.
- Key practical delta: with 40–60% cache hit and 8–16 token batching, Redwood's effective per-1M token economic can be materially lower for conversational workloads.

Numbers we discussed (ballpark estimates — we will run empirical tests next week):
- Hyperscaler managed endpoint (no cache, conservative batching): ~ $22–28 per 1M tokens.
- Redwood hosted (no cache): ~ $16–20 per 1M tokens.
- Redwood w/ realistic batching (avg batch 12) + 50% cache hit: ~ $8–11 per 1M tokens (this is where most savings show up).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity) further pushes unit economics down for sustained load; we can model tiers in the attached spreadsheet.

Proposed empirical tests (we should agree on exact datasets and metrics):
1) Throughput & latency run — 24h synthetic traffic at targeted qps profile (we suggest 200 qps max with peaks to 350 qps for 5 min windows). Measure p50/p90/p99 latencies and tail behaviour.
2) Cache effectiveness test — feed a representative 48-hour sample of your real prompt set to measure prefix/KV cache hit rate and resulting token reduction.
3) Cost profile test — use our test harness to simulate batching patterns and collect per-token cost under different cache hit scenarios (0%, 30%, 60%).

Immediate next steps / timeline:
- Rafael to share the test harness and small runbook today (attached).
- Finlytics to drop a 48-hour sample prompt file to the Drive link by EOD Tuesday (we'll treat data as non-sensitive; if you prefer a secure upload, Rafael will open a presigned bucket).
- Schedule the first 24h throughput run for Thursday 7/1 — Rafael/Neha will coordinate dial-in and monitoring.
- We'll produce a one-page cost/TCO memo within 48h of the runs.

Attachments: redwood-cost-model-v1.xlsx (cost model), redwood-test-harness-runbook.md (how we run tests).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Rafael for the technical details and to get the harness set up.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Thanks Neha — this is clear and helpful. A few quick clarifications before we hand a sample dataset to you: 

- Quantized variants: can you confirm whether the quantized 7B model you ran today is the same generation (weights) as the float baseline? In other vendors we've seen quality deltas when switching quantized variants.
- Cache TTL / eviction: what's the default prefix-cache TTL and do we control eviction windows? For our session rehydration patterns, TTL matters.
- Billing/POC: procurement wants a very rough 3-month PoC estimate (total expected spend) to include in our internal request. Can you give a preliminary top-line number (hosted vs dedicated) assuming our projected 1.2M tokens/day with 45% cache hit?

We can upload a stripped 48-hour sampling of prompts (PII scrubbed) by Tuesday; I'll put it in the Drive link you listed.

—James

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: James Liao <james.liao@finlytics.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Finlytics perf & economics — proposed tests and timelines

Hey James — quick technical answers and the numbers Neha promised.

Quantized variants / quality:
- The quantized 7B we used in the demo is a post-training 4-bit quant (GPTQ-style) derived from the same base weights as the float 7B we showed. For most instruction-style workloads we expect negligible quality regression; we recommend you include your high-sensitivity prompts in the test set so we can flag any regressions.

Prefix cache TTL & controls:
- Default prefix cache TTL is 48h, configurable per-route (can be set down to 5m or up to 7d). Eviction is LRU by default; we can enable a pinned-key set for hot prefixes if you prefer determinism.

Preliminary 3-month PoC cost sketch (assumptions: 1.2M tokens/day; 45% cache hit; avg batch size 10; all hosted numbers are post our small introductory credit and include standard network/infra surcharge):
- Redwood hosted (mixed quantized variants, auto-batching): ~ $9–11 per 1M effective tokens => ~ $300–350k over 90 days (includes some burst capacity).
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, committed baseline): ~ $5–7 per 1M effective tokens => ~ $170–210k over 90 days (requires a small monthly commitment).
- Hyperscaler managed endpoint (conservative estimate without app-level caching): ~ $18–24 per 1M effective tokens => ~ $540–720k over 90 days.

Important: those are directional estimates to help procurement. The attached cost model has sliders for cache hit rate and batching — small changes in those two variables create large delta. We'll run the empirical runs and produce a validated TCO after.

Recommended test plan (operational detail):
1) You upload your 48-hour scrubbed set to the Drive link.
2) We run a controlled 24h throughput run targeting your qps profile — we capture per-route token counts, batch size distribution, and the KV cache hit rate.
3) We replay a second run with identical inputs but force cache=0 to measure raw token delta.

I’m attaching the runbook and a tiny example of aggregated logs (example-logs-agg.txt) so your infra team can see the metric names we emit.

If you can confirm Tuesday upload and Thursday run, I’ll reserve the test window and provision a dedicated small pool for deterministic results.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
